1-1-1.title: Bhagavad Gita: Karma Yoga and Equanimity
1-1-1.explanation: The supplied NET source presents the Bhagavad Gita as a psychological-spiritual framework centred on action, self-knowledge and disciplined engagement with duty. Karma Yoga emphasises action without performance anxiety or attachment to the fruits of action; the broader Gita framework also links works, knowledge and devotion. A key exam distinction is The key NET distinction is not simply 'do your duty'. The source connects action with reduced attachment to outcomes and places Karma Yoga alongside knowledge and devotion as complementary paths. For exam application, If a PYQ contrasts action performed without greed for its fruits with non-performance of duty, retrieve Nishkama Karma within Karma Yoga. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are duty/action without attachment to fruits, Jnanayoga, Bhakti Yoga, equanimity and self-knowledge.

1-1-2.title: Buddhism
1-1-2.explanation: The supplied NET source presents Buddhism through the problem of suffering and the route toward its cessation. The Four Noble Truths identify suffering, its cause in craving/attachment, the possibility of cessation, and the path toward cessation; the Eightfold Path is described as a Middle Way between indulgence and severe asceticism. A key exam distinction is Do not reduce Buddhism in this syllabus to a list of moral rules. The exam-relevant structure is a causal sequence: suffering → its source → possibility of cessation → path. For exam application, When a stem asks for the truth concerning cessation or the path to cessation, distinguish Nirodha from Magga. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are Eightfold Path / Middle Way, nirvana.

1-1-3.explanation: The supplied NET source describes Sufism as the inner or esoteric dimension of Islam, with an emphasis on purification and direct experience. It distinguishes Shariah as the outer ethical/religious framework, Tariqah as the inner path and practice under guidance, and Haqiqah as direct experience of truth. A key exam distinction is The useful NET distinction is outer practice versus inner transformation: Shariah provides the external framework, Tariqah the path/practice, and Haqiqah the direct realisation of truth. For exam application, If a question asks which term refers to the inner path or direct mystical experience, retrieve Tariqah or Haqiqah respectively. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are inner dimension of Islam, nafs / self.

Its defining emphasis in the supplied source is synthesis and transformation of the entire being. For exam application, When the stem stresses harmonious development of all aspects of the person or transformation of ordinary consciousness, retrieve Integral Yoga. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are whole-person transformation, physical, vital, mental, psychic, spiritual, integrated consciousness.

1-2-1.title: Pre-independence era
1-2-1.explanation: Formal psychology education in India began in the early 20th century within a colonial education system. The uploaded NET material traces an important institutional beginning to Calcutta University: Sir Asutosh Mukherjee promoted Experimental Psychology in the postgraduate curriculum; Brojendra Nath Seal prepared the 1905 syllabus and established a laboratory. The laboratory was later upgraded into the first Department of Experimental Psychology. Research there included depth perception, psychophysics and attention. Psychology was included as a separate section of the Indian Science Congress in 1923; the Indian Psychological Association was founded in 1924 and the Indian Journal of Psychology appeared in 1925. 1-2-2.title: Post-independence era
1-2-2.explanation: The source describes post-independence psychology as expanding institutionally while remaining strongly influenced by its philosophical and Western scientific inheritance. After 1947, psychology was linked with nation-building and research. Departments expanded in universities such as Mysore and Patna; the University Grants Commission, established in 1956, supported university development. Applied and clinical psychology also expanded through institutions including NCERT and mental-health centres. The source notes that many psychology departments had emerged from philosophy departments, creating a continuing tension between philosophical roots and the aspiration to establish psychology as an experimental science. 1-2-3.title: 1970s social issues
1-2-3.explanation: During the 1970s, the source describes a shift toward socially relevant psychological research. Concerns included communal violence, social conflict and problems that were difficult to understand through culturally neutral laboratory approaches alone. The UNESCO-supported work associated with Gardner Murphy investigated communal violence and culminated in the 1953 volume In the Minds of Men; the later historical account presents this tradition as part of psychology's growing engagement with Indian social problems. The period also contributed to criticism that psychology should address the realities of Indian society rather than simply reproduce Western research. 1-2-4.explanation: Indigenization is presented as a move toward developing psychology that is sensitive to the cultural and historical conditions of the society in which it is practiced. D. Sinha's account distinguishes two facets: culture-bound concepts and categories, and the interaction of cultural variables with concepts, theories and methods introduced from outside. J. B. P. Sinha later described these as endogenous and exogenous indigenization. The source also gives examples of Indian psychologists developing or studying culturally grounded concepts and practices. 1-5-1.title: Structuralism
1-5-1.explanation: Structuralism treated conscious experience as something that could be analysed into basic elements, using introspection as its central method. Edward Titchener is the key NET association; he brought structuralism to the United States. A key exam distinction is Structuralism asks what conscious experience is made of; functionalism asks what mental processes do and how they help adaptation. Wundt's work and Titchener's structuralism should not be treated as identical. For exam application, A question describes analysing conscious experience into elementary components through introspection. Identify the school and theorist before looking at the options. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are elements of conscious experience, analysis of mental structure.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Wundt and Titchener are not identical in every respect.

1-5-2.title: Functionalism
1-5-2.explanation: Functionalism shifted attention from analysing the contents of consciousness to the functions of mental activity and behaviour. William James is the central association. The approach asks how mind and behaviour help people function, adapt and respond to their surroundings. A key exam distinction is Functionalism is not the search for the elements of consciousness. That emphasis belongs to structuralism. James was interested in how consciousness operates in real life and in adaptation. For exam application, If a PYQ asks which school is concerned with how the mind helps a person adapt, think William James and functionalism as the first retrieval cue. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are functions of mind, everyday functioning.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Functionalism asks about function, not just elements.

1-5-3.title: Psychoanalytical psychology
1-5-3.explanation: Psychoanalytical psychology, as presented in the supplied sources, centres on unconscious processes, conflict and the influence of repressed wishes and experiences on behaviour. Freud's model includes id, ego and superego; psychoanalysis aims to bring repressed unconscious material into consciousness and develop insight. A key exam distinction is Do not confuse repression with rationalization. Repression removes threatening material from conscious awareness, whereas rationalization supplies a rational-sounding explanation for a failure or transgression. For exam application, If a stem describes symptoms as indirect expressions of repressed wishes or asks about bringing unconscious material into consciousness, retrieve the psychoanalytic framework. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are id, ego, superego, pleasure principle.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Do not reduce psychoanalysis to one motive.

1-5-4.title: Gestalt psychology
1-5-4.explanation: Gestalt psychology argues that psychological experience, especially perception, cannot always be understood by simply adding isolated sensory elements. The organised pattern or whole matters. Wertheimer, Koffka and Köhler are central figures. A key exam distinction is The key contrast is whole versus isolated elements. Structuralism analyses elements; Gestalt psychology emphasizes the organisation and pattern in which those elements are experienced. For exam application, When a question describes a melody, visual pattern or apparent movement whose experience depends on the relationship among parts, identify the Gestalt principle rather than an element-by-element analysis. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are organized whole, pattern/configuration, insight learning.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Gestalt is broader than insight learning.

1-5-5.title: Behaviorism
1-5-5.explanation: Behaviorism redirected psychology toward observable behaviour and away from treating private consciousness as the primary scientific object. John B. Watson is the central founding figure in the classical school; later behaviourism developed conditioning and reinforcement traditions. A key exam distinction is Behaviorism is not structuralism's analysis of conscious experience. Watson argued that psychology should study behaviour itself rather than an unobservable mind or consciousness. For exam application, A stem says psychology should focus on observable behaviour rather than consciousness. The defining cue points to Watsonian behaviorism. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are stimulus-response.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Negative reinforcement increases behavior.

1-5-6.title: Humanistic-Existential psychology
1-5-6.explanation: The supplied NET framework treats Humanistic-Existential psychology as a major reaction against narrow accounts of people. Its emphasis is on subjective experience, meaning, agency, personal growth and the individual's relationship with existence rather than reducing behaviour to only observable responses or unconscious drives. A key exam distinction is The key contrast is emphasis: behaviorism foregrounds observable behaviour; psychoanalysis foregrounds unconscious conflict; humanistic-existential approaches foreground lived experience, agency, meaning and growth. For exam application, When a question highlights authenticity, personal meaning, choice, self-development or lived experience, retrieve the humanistic-existential orientation. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are existential choice, reaction against reductionism.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Humanistic psychology is not merely positive thinking.

1-5-7.title: Transpersonal psychology
1-5-7.explanation: The supplied NET framework places Transpersonal psychology among approaches that extend psychological inquiry beyond ordinary personal identity and include altered or expanded states of consciousness and spiritual dimensions of experience. In the supplied Indian-psychology material, consciousness and self-knowledge are also central themes, making the distinction between transpersonal and mainstream personal-level accounts especially important. A key exam distinction is Do not collapse transpersonal psychology into religion. The psychological emphasis is on experiences and states that extend beyond ordinary personal identity and on their possible relation to consciousness and self-development. For exam application, When a stem focuses on transcending ordinary identity or studying expanded states of consciousness, retrieve the transpersonal orientation. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are expanded consciousness, transcendence, altered states.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: It is not identical to any single religion.

4-2-1.title: Neuron structure
4-2-1.explanation: A neuron is a specialised information-processing and information-transmitting cell. Its major structural regions are the soma (cell body), dendrites, axon and terminal buttons. Dendrites generally receive incoming information, the soma maintains the cell and integrates inputs, and the axon carries the neural message toward terminal regions. A key exam distinction is Dendrites and axons have different typical directions of information flow: dendrites receive toward the cell body, whereas the axon carries the neural message away toward terminals. Myelin insulates axons and can increase conduction speed. For exam application, For a structure-function question, map the part to its role: dendrite = receiving, soma = cell body, axon = conducting, terminal = communicating with the next cell. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are axon terminals.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Dendrites and axons have different typical roles.

4-2-3.title: Types of neurons
4-2-3.explanation: Neurons can be distinguished by their role in information flow. Sensory (afferent) neurons carry information toward the central nervous system, motor (efferent) neurons carry commands away from the CNS to effectors, and interneurons connect neural pathways within the CNS. A key exam distinction is Afferent means toward the CNS; efferent means away from the CNS. The distinction is about direction of information flow, not whether a neuron is physically located in the brain or spinal cord. For exam application, If a PYQ asks whether a pathway carries sensory information toward the CNS or motor commands away from it, use the afferent/efferent direction rule first. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are sensory/afferent, motor/efferent.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Afferent/efferent are defined relative to the CNS.

4-2-4.title: Neural impulse
4-2-4.explanation: Neural signalling within an axon depends on changes in membrane potential. At rest the neuron maintains a resting potential; sufficient stimulation reaches threshold and initiates an action potential. Depolarization is followed by repolarization and a refractory phase. A key exam distinction is An action potential is not graded in amplitude: once threshold is reached, the action potential follows an all-or-none pattern. In myelinated axons, saltatory conduction makes the signal appear to jump between nodes of Ranvier. For exam application, When a question asks what happens after threshold, retrieve the sequence: depolarization → repolarization → refractory period.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Stimulus intensity is not coded by larger action potentials.

4-2-5.title: Synaptic transmission
4-2-5.explanation: Communication between neurons occurs across a synapse rather than by direct physical continuity. An action potential reaching the axon terminal triggers processes that allow neurotransmitter substances to be released into the synaptic cleft and influence the receiving cell. A key exam distinction is Neural impulse refers to electrical signalling within the neuron; synaptic transmission concerns communication from one cell to another across the synaptic gap. Do not treat these as identical processes. For exam application, If a stem moves from an action potential at the terminal to release of a chemical messenger and its effect on another cell, the tested concept is synaptic transmission.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: A neurotransmitter's effect depends on its receptor/context.

5-10-3.title: Related issues in classical conditioning
5-10-3.explanation: Related issues in classical conditioning include processes such as acquisition, extinction, stimulus generalization and discrimination, and spontaneous recovery. These phenomena concern how conditioned responses are established, weakened, generalized or recovered over time. Acquisition is the development of a conditioned response; Extinction follows when the conditioned stimulus is no longer paired with the unconditioned stimulus; Generalization extends responding to similar stimuli; Discrimination involves learning to respond differently to distinct stimuli; spontaneous recovery is the return of an extinguished response after a delay; SOURCE BASIS; Ciccarelli & White 6e — Classical Conditioning; Self-Teaching Guide — conditioning phenomena; PowerWithin Psychology. 5-10-3.source_notes: Kaplan extends classical conditioning beyond the basic Pavlovian sequence to expectancy, biological preparedness and taste aversion. These examples are useful for questions asking when conditioning is not a simple equal-pairing process.
